# riftnation

Open-source community-first marketplace for Riftbound TCG trading in Dubai / UAE. The codebase starts with a NestJS Catalog bounded context that syncs the official Riftbound card catalog into Postgres; listings, collections, payments, and decentralized settlement layers will come in later bounded contexts.

## Project overview

Riftnation is an open-source marketplace aimed at the UAE Riftbound
community. The first bounded context is **catalog**: a NestJS module
that syncs official card data (from the public Riftbound card gallery
page) into Postgres on a daily schedule, then exposes normalized
card queries for downstream contexts. A companion GitHub Actions cron
runs the sync at 11:00 Asia/Dubai daily.

Future bounded contexts (listings, collections, pricing, payments)
will live in their own modules inside the same NestJS monolith until
a split is justified.

## Coding conventions

- TypeScript strict mode; no `any` unless unavoidable at an adapter
  boundary with a local ESLint disable comment explaining why.
- Follow DDD layering inside each bounded context: `domain/`,
  `application/`, `infrastructure/`, `api/`. I/O lives at the edges;
  `domain/` has zero imports from `infrastructure/` or `api/`.
- Value objects guard invariants at the domain boundary. Prefer them
  over primitive types in aggregate state.
- Tests live next to the code: `foo.ts` + `foo.spec.ts`. Integration
  tests that need Postgres use `@testcontainers/postgresql`.
- Write the failing test first, then the minimal implementation that
  makes it pass, then commit.
- Never hard-delete rows in the catalog tables; tombstone via
  `deleted_at` and restore when upstream re-publishes a record.

## Commit discipline

- One concern per commit.
- Subject line ≤ 72 chars, imperative mood, Conventional-Commit
  prefix when it fits (`feat`, `fix`, `chore`, `docs`, `test`,
  `ci`, `refactor`).
- Body (when helpful) explains the *why*, not the *what*.
- Every commit ends with an `Assisted-by:` footer per the
  Attribution section. Human-only commits use `Assisted-by: n/a`.
- Never use `--no-verify` or `--amend` on a published commit
  without explicit user approval.

## Attribution

All commits must end with an `Assisted-by:` footer.

- AI-assisted: `Assisted-by: {agent}:{model}`
- Human-only: `Assisted-by: n/a`
- Multiple footers are allowed for multi-vendor work.
